question: What relative lengths are shown in Figure 6B-2 for a merging taper, shifting taper, and shoulder taper?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 6B-2 labels the merging taper as having a length of L, each shifting taper as ½ L, and the shoulder taper as ⅓ L. This matches Table 6B-3, which lists a merging taper as "at least L," a shifting taper as "at least 0.5 L," and a shoulder taper as "at least 0.33 L," with L calculated using the formulas in Table 6B-4. Guidance (recommended): - "The appropriate taper length (L) should be determined using the criteria shown in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4." - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." Options (permitted): - The lateral buffer space may be used to separate the traffic space from the work space, as shown in Figures 6B-1 and 6B-2; a note on the figure indicates "*S = speed in mph" and "See Table 6B-4 for formulas for calculating taper length (L)." Support (informational): - Types of tapers are shown in Figure 6B-2; the accompanying taper-length table lists "Merging Taper — at least L" and "Shifting Taper — at least 0.5 L." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6B-2 depicts a merging taper dimensioned as "L," shifting tapers dimensioned as "1/2 L" (on both the median and shoulder sides), and a shoulder taper dimensioned as "1/3 L," along with an optional downstream taper. [Image 2] Table 6B-3 lists taper lengths of "at least L" (merging), "at least 0.5 L" (shifting), "at least 0.33 L" (shoulder), and 50–100 feet for one-lane, two-way and downstream tapers. [Image 3] The full-page view of Figure 6B-2 (p.774) confirms the L, ½ L, and ⅓ L dimensioning of the merging, shifting, and shoulder tapers. [Image 4] Page 776 presents the Guidance provisions stating shifting tapers should be approximately ½ L and shoulder tapers approximately ⅓ L. [Image 5] Figure 6B-3 (p.777) illustrates the related one-lane, two-way traffic taper and downstream taper at 50 to 100 ft. [Image 6] Figure 6P-38 (p.935) shows a shoulder taper and tapers dimensioned with L and ½ L in a typical application, consistent with Figure 6B-2. gold_answer: Merging taper: L; shifting taper: 1/2 L; shoulder taper: 1/3 L.
